summary: Most visitors need a Liberian visa arranged before travel — through an embassy or Liberia's online eVisa channel — while citizens of the 15 ECOWAS countries enter visa-free under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of all arriving travelers and is checked at Roberts International Airport.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but medical coverage including evacuation is strongly advised — hospital care in Liberia is very limited and serious cases are evacuated abroad.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia

onwardTicket.text: Airlines flying into Monrovia commonly require a confirmed return or onward ticket, and visa applications ask for travel itineraries.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia

currencyLimits.text: Cash of USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) should be declared on arrival and departure. Confirm current thresholds with a Liberian embassy before carrying large sums.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Liberia

payments.text: The US dollar circulates alongside the Liberian dollar and is accepted everywhere. Bring US dollars in cash. Cards work only at a handful of Monrovia hotels, and ATMs dispensing US dollars are scarce.

safety.text: Liberia is stable but poor, with opportunistic street crime in Monrovia. Avoid displaying valuables, use trusted drivers after dark, and remember that emergency services and medical care are minimal.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Liberia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to April is the dry season and the practical window for travel — Monrovia is one of the world's wettest capitals, and the May–October rains flood roads across the country.

idp.text: Liberia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties
source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: Liberia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Liberia yet.

source.name: UN Treaty Collection — Convention on Road Traffic (Vienna, 1968), status of parties

tips.text: Bring clean, recent US dollar notes. They are legal tender alongside the Liberian dollar and by far the most practical way to pay; torn or pre-2009 bills are often refused.
From May to October Liberia gets some of the heaviest rainfall on earth — up-country roads become impassable and flights are disrupted, so plan travel for the November–April dry season.
Your yellow fever certificate is checked at Roberts International Airport — travelers without one risk vaccination on the spot at a fee or refusal of entry.
Liberia uses US-style 120 V sockets (types A and B) — unusual for Africa — and mains power is unreliable, so pack a power bank and check chargers for dual voltage.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Liberia?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Visas are issued in advance by Liberian embassies, and an online eVisa channel has been introduced. Confirm the current online option with the nearest mission. Citizens of the 15 ECOWAS countries enter visa-free under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Liberia?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders must obtain a visa before travel from a Liberian embassy or consulate; fees for US applicants are set on a reciprocity basis. There is no visa on arrival for tourists.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Liberia?
faq.answer: No — tourists cannot rely on a visa on arrival. Arrange your visa before travel through an embassy or Liberia's eVisa channel; airlines will normally refuse boarding without one.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Liberia?
faq.answer: Yes. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of all arriving travelers regardless of nationality, and it is checked on arrival.

faq.question: What currency should I bring to Liberia?
faq.answer: US dollars in cash. The US dollar is used alongside the Liberian dollar for everyday payments, cards are accepted almost nowhere, and ATMs are unreliable. Bring enough clean, recent US notes for your whole stay.
